principle: Diagnose the problem before proposing the solution.
mechanism: Premature solutions bake in untested assumptions about what is actually broken.
use_when: product feedback | feature requests | teardown friction
diagnostic_questions: What user problem is the proposed feature actually solving? | What evidence says that is the problem rather than one possible solution?
landmine: Turning feedback directly into features.
supporting_guests: Ian McAllister | Bill Carr | Marty Cagan | Dharmesh Shah | Laura Schaffer

principle: Define the target user and outcome before synthesizing conflicting feedback.
mechanism: Feedback only becomes comparable when it is interpreted against the same user and outcome.
use_when: conflicting stakeholder feedback | broad products | segmentation
diagnostic_questions: Who exactly is the target user? | Which problem matters most for that user? | Which feedback is irrelevant for this target?
landmine: Averaging contradictory feedback into a compromised product.
supporting_guests: Julie Zhuo | Annie Pearl | Jake Knapp | Daniel Lereya

principle: Retention among users who reach core value is stronger evidence of product-market fit than acquisition alone.
mechanism: Acquisition or signup can mask weak value; retention after value exposure is harder to fake.
diagnostic_questions: Which users have actually experienced core value? | Do those users retain? | If onboarding friction vanished, would the product itself still be compelling?
landmine: Mistaking acquisition or onboarding completion for product-market fit.
supporting_guests: Sean Ellis | Todd Jackson | Nikita Bier | Gustaf Alströmer

principle: Do not pour acquisition into a leaky product before fixing product-market fit and retention.
mechanism: More top-of-funnel volume amplifies downstream leakage instead of creating durable growth.
use_when: growth planning | demand generation | funnel diagnosis
diagnostic_questions: Where is the largest leak in the funnel? | Are retained users satisfied enough to justify scaling acquisition?
landmine: Hiring demand generation to compensate for weak product-market fit.
supporting_guests: Krithika Shankarraman | Todd Jackson

principle: Define activation around the moment a user experiences value, then design onboarding backward from it.
mechanism: A concrete value event gives the team a goalpost for removing friction and accelerating learning.
diagnostic_questions: What is the aha moment? | What behavior best predicts later retention? | How quickly can a new user reach it?
landmine: Optimizing onboarding completion instead of value realization.
supporting_guests: Hila Qu | Ben Williams | Sean Ellis | Lauryn Isford

principle: Shorten time-to-value by letting users experience useful behavior before requiring full understanding or setup.
mechanism: Hands-on value creates understanding faster than explanation-heavy onboarding.
diagnostic_questions: Can users experience value with a template, sample, or warm start? | What setup can be deferred?
landmine: Teaching the product before letting users use it.
supporting_guests: Lauryn Isford | Shishir Mehrotra | Hila Qu

principle: Judge retention with cohorts and curves, not just aggregate engagement.
mechanism: Aggregate usage can hide whether successive cohorts are stabilizing, decaying, or improving.
diagnostic_questions: Where does the retention curve flatten? | Are newer cohorts better than older ones? | Which retained behavior represents recurring value?
landmine: Using DAU/MAU or total usage as proof of retention quality.
supporting_guests: Josh Miller | Brian Balfour | Elena Verna | Adam Fishman

principle: Treat distribution as a product constraint, not a post-launch marketing task.
mechanism: A product whose natural users cannot discover, adopt, or share it has a structurally weaker growth model.
diagnostic_questions: Where do target users already spend attention? | What behavior creates the next user? | Does the product itself create distribution?
landmine: Building a product first and assuming acquisition can be bolted on later.
supporting_guests: Elena Verna | Luc Levesque | Casey Winters | Manik Gupta

principle: Prefer pricing metrics that rise with customer value when the product supports a credible value-linked unit.
mechanism: The unit you charge on shapes expansion, willingness to pay, and whether customer success aligns with vendor revenue.
diagnostic_questions: What unit best tracks customer value? | Does customer success naturally increase what they pay? | Can the metric be understood and predicted?
landmine: Choosing a convenient billing unit that is disconnected from value.
supporting_guests: Patrick Campbell | Madhavan Ramanujam | Julia Schottenstein | Eoghan McCabe

principle: Pricing is part of strategy, not an independent knob.
mechanism: Price changes alter positioning, target customer, sales motion, product expectations, and competitive set.
diagnostic_questions: If price changes, what else in the strategy must change? | Which customer segment does this price imply?
landmine: Optimizing price in isolation from product and go-to-market.
supporting_guests: Jason Cohen | Melissa Tan | Jeanne DeWitt Grosser | Shishir Mehrotra

principle: Your product architecture often determines whether the motion can be product-led or must be sales-led.
mechanism: Required permissions, integrations, security, and buyer authority can force an enterprise buying motion regardless of growth preference.
diagnostic_questions: Can an individual user adopt without executive approval? | Does setup require privileged integrations or sensitive data access? | Who uses, buys, and approves?
landmine: Choosing PLG because it is fashionable when adoption structurally requires top-down approval.
supporting_guests: Eeke de Milliano | Shishir Mehrotra | Claire Vo | Elena Verna | Merci Grace

principle: Fix positioning before rewriting the sales pitch.
mechanism: A weak pitch is often downstream of an unclear differentiated value proposition.
diagnostic_questions: Can the target customer explain why this is different? | Is the value proposition specific to a competitive alternative?
landmine: Treating messaging symptoms while leaving positioning ambiguous.
supporting_guests: April Dunford | Rahul Vohra

principle: Prioritization is primarily the discipline of saying no to work that dilutes the critical journey.
mechanism: Every additional feature creates product, cognitive, and maintenance surface area; value does not scale linearly with feature count.
diagnostic_questions: Which user journey must be exceptional? | What would break if we did not build this? | What existing complexity does this add to?
landmine: Equating responsiveness to requests with product quality.
supporting_guests: Manik Gupta | Melissa Perri | Marty Cagan | Ian McAllister

principle: Strategy is a set of choices about where to concentrate advantage, not a list of initiatives.
mechanism: A strategy becomes useful when it makes some attractive options explicitly less important than the chosen path.
use_when: strategy reviews | roadmap planning | competitive analysis
diagnostic_questions: What are we choosing to win on? | What are we explicitly not doing? | What must be true for this choice to work?
landmine: Calling a roadmap or aspiration a strategy.
supporting_guests: Georgiana Laudi | Jason Shah | Ravi Mehta

principle: Turn strategic uncertainty into explicit hypotheses you can test quickly.
mechanism: Fast, structured experiments convert abstract debate into evidence and make strategy adaptive rather than rhetorical.
diagnostic_questions: What assumption determines whether this strategy works? | What is the cheapest credible test? | What result changes the decision?
landmine: Using strategy frameworks to avoid testing assumptions.
supporting_guests: Mayur Kamat | Christina Wodtke | Yuriy Timen

principle: Product quality requires explicit end-to-end ownership and a team-level quality bar, not just final-stage polish.
mechanism: Quality degrades when nobody feels accountable for the whole experience, even if individual requirements are met.
use_when: product quality | design critique | mature products
diagnostic_questions: Who is accountable for the end-to-end experience? | What quality bar would the team defend even if metrics were neutral?
landmine: Treating quality as polish delegated to design at the end.
supporting_guests: Tobi Lütke | Karri Saarinen | Katie Dill

principle: Treat speed, quality, and cost as a context-dependent tension: strong teams can improve more than one, but cannot assume tradeoffs disappear.
mechanism: Cutting corners creates rework, while better judgment, tooling, and smaller tests reduce cycle time without degrading the product.
use_when: shipping velocity | MVP debates | engineering/product execution
diagnostic_questions: What is actually slowing learning? | Which work is waste versus necessary quality? | Can we reduce scope without reducing integrity?
landmine: Using urgency as permission for sloppy product decisions.
supporting_guests: Wes Kao | Gustaf Alströmer | Nickey Skarstad

principle: Use competitor patterns to learn conventions and mechanisms, not as a blueprint for what your product should become.
mechanism: Competitive patterns can reveal established interaction conventions, but copying them imports assumptions that may not fit your users or advantage.
use_when: competitive teardowns | feature design | mature categories
diagnostic_questions: What pattern is common across competitors? | Why does it exist? | Which parts apply to our user and which do not?
landmine: Copying a competitor feature without understanding its mechanism.
supporting_guests: Elena Verna

principle: Treat an AI prototype as evidence of possibility, not production readiness; validate reliability, domain correctness, observability, and failure modes.
mechanism: AI systems behave probabilistically and encounter long-tail inputs that prototypes do not expose.
diagnostic_questions: What can the model reliably do today? | Which failures matter most? | Which subject-matter experts define correctness? | How will failures be observed?
landmine: Assuming a vibe-coded prototype proves production feasibility.
supporting_guests: Aishwarya Naresh Reganti | Elizabeth Stone

principle: Use human review when AI errors are costly or hard to verify; reduce it when outputs can be reliably checked or automated safeguards are sufficient.
mechanism: Human review provides judgment, escalation, and feedback where model confidence is insufficient.
diagnostic_questions: What decisions can AI make autonomously? | What confidence or risk threshold triggers review? | How does human feedback improve the system?
landmine: Promoting a copilot to autopilot without defining failure boundaries.
supporting_guests: Inbal Shani | Aishwarya Naresh Reganti
